title: Task Envelope v1
description: Standard input contract of the Runtime Task Bus (Plan 6). Every task stored in the Task Bus database (runtime/tasks.db, input_json column) must be a complete Task Envelope matching this schema. Callers dispatch tasks by route; the Task Bus resolves the target Agent role from framework-config/routing.yaml. Callers must NOT guess or specify the target Agent directly.

schema_version.description: Envelope schema version. Fixed to 1 for Task Envelope v1. Any breaking schema change must bump this value (see templates/AGENTS.md).

task_id.description: Unique task identifier, generated by the Task Bus runtime when the task is created (crypto.randomUUID() or the runtime's native equivalent). Callers may omit task_id when submitting a new task; the Task Bus fills it in before persisting the complete envelope into input_json. Timestamp-only IDs that can collide are forbidden. Not human-readable by requirement.

parent_task_id.description: Optional reference to the parent task_id for main-task -> sub-task relationships. Plan 6 only records this field; it does NOT automatically build a full DAG from it.

project_id.description: Target business project identifier. Must exist in framework-config/projects.yaml.

route.description: Task route name. Must come from framework-config/routing.yaml routes (e.g. code_read, project_analysis, project_coordination, code_change, database_read, database_write, database_ddl, database_backup, api_code_change, api_runtime_call, api_regression, build_and_test, independent_review, session_lifecycle, documentation_update, long_term_memory_write). The Task Bus resolves the target role from the route; callers must not specify the target Agent directly.

objective.description: The final goal of the task, expressed as a string.

constraints.description: List of constraints the executor must respect (e.g. scope limits, forbidden operations).

dependencies.description: Array of other task_id values that must be COMPLETED before this task can run. Plan 6 implements only a dependency readiness guard (BLOCKED until dependencies are satisfied); there is no automatic DAG scheduler.

expected_output.description: List describing the content the caller expects to receive back.

acceptance_criteria.description: List of conditions that define when the task is considered done.

context_refs.description: Lightweight references only, such as mem0:<memory-id>, git:current-diff, task:<task-id>, or doc:<path>. Do NOT embed large payloads (e.g. hundreds of KB of full source code) inside the Task Envelope; reference them instead.

metadata.description: Reserved extension object for additional non-standard fields. Must not contain credentials of any kind (passwords, API keys, database credentials, tokens, secrets).
